headline: Smell bypasses rational thought and goes directly to memory and emotion centers
universal_truth: Our oldest senses often speak to us in ways our newest thoughts cannot
fun_facts: Smell is processed by the limbic system—the same brain area that handles memory and emotion
Humans can distinguish over 1 trillion different scents
A scent can trigger a vivid memory decades old, complete with emotions—this is called the Proust effect
discussion_questions: What scent immediately transports you to a specific memory?
Why might smell be more connected to emotion than vision or hearing?
How do marketers and businesses use scent to influence you?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: A whiff of sunscreen and you're at the beach at age eight. Grandma's perfume and she's suddenly present again. No other sense does this—instantly transporting you through time, complete with emotions. Smell is the time-travel sense.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: You see a photo and remember something. You hear an old song and feel nostalgic. But smell? Smell doesn't remind you of a memory—it drops you into it. Why is smell so uniquely powerful for memory?
cliff.prompt: Why does smell trigger such vivid memories?

options.text: Smell signals go directly to the limbic system—the brain's memory and emotion center
options.response: Yes. Smell bypasses the rational brain and connects directly to where memories and emotions live.

options.text: Smell was our first sense, so it has the oldest pathways in the brain
options.response: Smell is ancient, but the key is its direct limbic connection...

q1.title: The Direct Line
q1.script: Most senses route through the thalamus before reaching other brain areas. Smell is different—it goes directly to the olfactory bulb, connected straight to the amygdala and hippocampus. Memory and emotion centers get smell signals with no middleman.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "The Direct Line"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: One Trillion Scents
q2.script: Recent research shows humans can distinguish over 1 trillion different scents. We have about 400 types of scent receptors that combine in patterns, like letters forming words. Your nose reads a chemical vocabulary more complex than language.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: The Proust Effect
q3.script: The Proust effect—named after a novelist who wrote about it—describes how a scent can trigger a vivid, emotional memory from decades ago. You don't just remember; you re-experience. Smell collapses time.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Our oldest senses speak in ways our newest thoughts cannot. Smell reminds us that we're connected to our past through channels that bypass logic. Honor the wisdom your body remembers.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 82. Tomorrow, we'll explore how skin feels things. Until then, seek out a scent from your past—and notice where it takes you.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Scent Journey - Time Travel Through Smell
growTrack.learning_objective: Use scent intentionally to access emotional memory
growTrack.activity: Find a scent connected to a positive memory—a perfume, a food, a place. Spend a moment with it. Notice how smell bypasses thought and drops you directly into feeling. Consider: how might you use scent intentionally for comfort or grounding?
